content: Rhamnose is a naturally occurring deoxy sugar. It can be categorized as either a methyl-pentose or a 6-deoxy-hexose. In nature, rhamnose is predominantly found in its L-form, known as L-rhamnose (6-deoxy-L-mannose). This is notable because most naturally occurring sugars exist in the D-form. Exceptions to this general rule include the methyl-pentoses L-fucose and L-rhamnose, as well as the pentose L-arabinose. L-rhamnose can be extracted from plants such as buckthorn (Rhamnus) and poison sumac. Additionally, it is commonly found as a glycoside in various other plant species. Rhamnose is also a structural component of the outer cell membrane of acid-fast bacteria belonging to the Mycobacterium genus, which includes the pathogen responsible for tuberculosis.
